title: Unknown positive currents preserved seven source ambiguities despite unequal capacitance in two partial adult worm models
abstract: We tested whether unequal cell capacitance identifies a hidden input when its waveform is unknown. Two partial adult C. elegans electrical maps had seven exact twin pairs. A 10 percent capacitance change gave different remote responses to equal known currents. A causal positive filter changed the input waveform and made every remote voltage identical. Both currents had equal total charge. Frequency residuals were below 6.1e-16. Independent time integration agreed within 4.9e-10 relative error. An all-pair audit found 26 pairs per map with one independent remote transfer pattern. We prove the rank test by block elimination and check 100 synthetic graphs. The result qualifies an earlier equal-current test. Partial wiring, assumed parameters, full remote observation and absent activity data limit biological use. Code, aggregate evidence, hashes and retrieval steps support reproduction. External records stay outside the bundle.

display.caption: Equal known currents give a remote contrast in seven twin pairs. A positive waveform filter removes that contrast. These are passive-model results.

citations.reason: We reproduce its equal-current contrast and test waveform uncertainty.
